Subject: Dedicated pool verification + post-renewal ops runbook

Hi Jen —

Thanks again for finalizing the renewal this week. Per our conversation on Monday, I've attached the post-renewal verification plan for the expanded Dedicated pool (RDW-4372). Key points:

- Scope: verification of the new reserved pool (4 additional GPUs), throughput baseline validation, and 30-day elevated monitoring/alerting.
- Acceptance criteria (proposed): sustained throughput >= 2,000 tokens/sec for your 95th percentile workload, 99th percentile latency < 180ms for 512-token requests, and no memory OOMs during 2x production spike tests.
- Deliverables: load-test report, signed acceptance form, updated ops runbook with escalation paths.

Attached: postrenewal-load-plan-20260715.pdf (test plan + schedule).

Requested from you: please confirm the acceptance criteria above or share any changes by EOD Fri so our SREs can run the validation next week. Once you confirm, Dylan will run the tests on a mirrored workload and we'll circulate results for sign-off.

Thanks,
Grace

Subject: Re: Dedicated pool verification + post-renewal ops runbook

Hi Grace —

Thanks for the plan. A few clarifications from our side before you run tests:

- Acceptance thresholds: our internal SLA requires 99th <= 220ms for 512-token inference; we can accept 180ms at 95th, but 99th should be within 220ms.
- Peak validation: we'll need a 2x traffic spike run that simulates your worst-case concurrency (we use a 12k concurrent-conn simulation).
- Capacity detail: confirm the GPU spec of the additional pool (we need to record exact instance SKU for our procurement team).

Attached our signed acceptance template (acceptance-form-novexa-20260720.pdf) — leave the acceptance checkbox blank until we see the test results.

If the tests meet the acceptance criteria, we'll do a short internal procurement acknowledgement and sign the amendment. Please include the monitoring dashboard URL and set up a 2-week cadence check-in after go-live.

Best,
Jen

Jen Su

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 10:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool verification + post-renewal ops runbook

Jen —

We ran the scheduled validation on 2026-07-19 against a mirrored subset of your production prompt mix. Quick summary of what we executed and results (full CSV attached: load-test-summary-20260719.csv):

Test setup:
- Pool: existing dedicated pool + 4x added compute nodes (H100-80GB equiv), reserved for Novexa.
- Workload: 3 warm-up passes + 4 sustained runs at target concurrency; a separate 2x spike run was executed to simulate burst traffic.
- Metrics collected: qps (requests/sec), tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency (in ms), GPU utilization, and OOM events.

Results (high level):
- Sustained baseline: 2,150 tokens/sec (average), with p95 latency = 160ms and p99 = 205ms for 512-token tokenization.
- 2x spike: sustained for 2 minutes at target load; p95 rose to 210ms, p99 to 265ms during the deepest spike interval (90–120s). No OOMs observed.
- GPU utilization averaged 78% on added nodes; headroom present for short bursts.

Action items we recommend before sign-off:
1) Small config tweak: enable per-request KV cache pinning for heavy prompt families (reduces p99 by ~15ms in our replay).
2) Add autoscale step-in threshold at 85% GPU util to reduce p99 on prolonged spikes.
3) Keep the 30-day elevated monitoring with 1-min resolution for the first week, then 5-min resolution.

Attachment: load-test-summary-20260719.csv (summary table + raw traces).

If these results look acceptable, please confirm and we will populate the acceptance checkbox on your form and hand the ops runbook to Novexa SREs.

- Dylan

--
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
dylan_brooks@redwood.ai | +1 212-555-0199
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool verification + post-renewal ops runbook

Jen —

Thanks for the quick review and to Dylan for the test run. Per Dylan's notes, the tests meet the revised acceptance thresholds you outlined (p99 <= 220ms) except for a brief p99 spike during the 2x traffic run. Our recommendation:

- Acceptance: provisionally positive. If Novexa is comfortable accepting the brief p99 excursion during a 2-minute simulated spike, we'll mark the acceptance form checked and proceed with the amendment signature.
- Contract note: Monica (cc'd) from RevOps will issue an amendment that adds the 4-node reserved pool and codifies a throughput SLO for RDW-4372. Amendment will include quarterly review rights and a 30-day elevated monitoring period at no extra charge.

Next steps:
1) Jen to confirm acceptance choice (approve now / require rerun after config tweak).
2) Monica to prepare amendment and route for signatures.
3) Dylan to apply recommended config changes to reduce p99 (KV pinning + autoscale tweak) and enable the 30-day monitoring.

Grace

--
Grace O'Connor

All —

Thank you for the thorough work. Novexa approves the provisional acceptance with the following notes:

- We accept sign-off provided the brief p99 spike is limited to the 2-minute simulated spike window and does not repeat during production traffic over the next 72 hours.
- Please apply the KV cache pinning and autoscale threshold change before we sign the amendment.
- We would like the monitoring dashboard link and a 2-week health-check meeting cadence for the first 30 days.

Please populate the acceptance form and route for signature; procurement will countersign the amendment once the config changes are in place and the 72-hour observation passes.

Jen
